name: Simon
overview: Simon was a male member of the tribe of Judah, noted in Scripture as a "brother" of Jesus and son of Mary. The term "brother" here is understood to mean that Simon and Jesus were born of the same womb, indicating a close familial bond. His identity is grounded primarily in this relationship within the family of Christ.
namesAndTitles: The name Simon is a proper name meaning "he has heard" or "obedient one." This name, recorded in Matthew 13:55, does not indicate that it was given by God but reflects a common Hebrew name of the period.
familyAndRelationships: Simon is explicitly identified as a brother of Jesus, the Messiah, and is inferred to be a son of Mary, the mother of Jesus. These relationships are based on the biblical reference in Matthew 13:55. Scripture does not provide further family details beyond these.
scriptureSignificance: Simon’s significance lies chiefly in his familial connection to Jesus, highlighting the humanity of Christ and His earthly family. Being a brother of Jesus born of the same mother, Simon represents the earthly kinship of the Savior. This relationship underscores the reality of Jesus’ incarnation and His participation in a genuine human family.
